title.value: The Eleven Days: Terrace Switching, Row Order and the Conduct of Negotiation at the Turning Ground of Half Light

abstract.value: Once each terrace cycle the Evening Band householders and the warren dwellers meet on neutral ground and spend eleven days exchanging row positions, storage rights and outstanding obligations in a single continuous negotiation. We describe the structure of the eleven days, the role of the sequence keeper, and the rule that no position may be exchanged twice within one meeting. Contrary to the usual assumption that such assemblies clear debts, the meeting reliably ends with more open obligations than it began with, and the participants regard this as its purpose. We suggest that the turning ground be classed as a debt-generating institution rather than a market.
